channel.description: Recent content in Research Projects on Guojia Wu

item.title: shRNAone & Cas13: High-Resolution RNA Knockdown Profiling
item.description:
• Contributed to the analysis and writing of a high-resolution comparative study of RNA-targeting systems in the Chul KWON Lab (School of Biomedical Sciences, HKU), and played a substantial role across the whole project.

  • The study developed shRNAone, an engineered shRNA scaffold that eliminates processing heterogeneity and guarantees guide biogenesis at single-nucleotide precision. It systematically decoupled microRNA seed and 3′ supplementary pairing rules using a library of 2,800 miRNA variants (SynthoMir), demonstrated that potent guides identified by single-nucleotide tiling screens directly translate into synthetic siRNA designs, and mapped the knockdown landscapes of shRNAone, CasRx, and PspCas13b across the identical mRNA — revealing that target RNA accessibility is a universal determinant of guide efficacy.

  • My work focused on computational analyses and manuscript writing, including high-throughput sequencing and pooled screening data analysis, parametrization of the RNA accessibility model (RNAplfold), and translation of the analyses into the manuscript.

item.title: Pan-Cancer Atlas of TCGA ipaQTM
item.description:
• Explored the impact of DNA methylation on intronic pre-mRNA polyadenylation (IPA) across 23 cancer types. Investigated how IPA, similar to alternative splicing, generates RNA isoforms with missing exons, potentially producing altered proteins relevant to cancer biology.
  • Constructed a pan-cancer ipaQTM map using TCGA methylation and transcriptome data. Performed cis- and trans-association analyses with Inpact and MatrixEQTL to link methylation sites to IPA events, identified over 500,000 significant associations, and pinpointed thousands of candidate IPA regulators including genes such as CCAR2, CPSF1, and ZC3H3, as well as regulatory effects involving DNA structure and transcription factor binding (e.g., CTCF).
  • Applied integrative computational approaches, including methylation-QTL mapping, transcriptomic analysis, and regulatory network inference, to systematically link DNA modifications with RNA processing events in cancer.

item.title: Comprehensive Benchmark of DNN-Based pMHC Predictors
item.description:
• Conducted a comprehensive benchmark of deep learning models for peptide-HLA (pMHC) binding prediction. Built an independent dataset of 290,000+ peptides across 44 alleles, carefully curated to avoid overlap with training sets, and used it as a gold-standard benchmark.
  • Systematically evaluated 17 state-of-the-art predictors, including conventional DNNs, attention-based architectures, and capsule networks. Compared predictive accuracy, robustness across alleles, and computational efficiency, and applied SHAP/LIME to dissect residue-level feature contributions. Found that self-attention models (STMHCpan, BigMHC) delivered the best overall performance, while models trained on eluted ligand data showed superior generalizability.
  • Applied a range of computational and experimental techniques, including dataset curation, deep learning model evaluation, and explainable AI analysis.

item.title: The role of HADH Isoform 3 in Endometrial Cancer
item.description:
• Investigated the tumor-suppressive role of HADH isoform 3 in endometrial cancer (EC). Found that isoform 3 is selectively downregulated in EC, and its loss activates EGFR-MEK/ERK signaling to promote tumor progression, suggesting biomarker and therapeutic potential.
  • Designed an independent project integrating computational and experimental approaches. Analyzed TCGA and GEO datasets to profile fatty acid metabolism genes, applied Lasso and survival-SVM models to identify HADH as a prognostic marker, and quantified isoform-specific expression with long-read RNA-seq. Established stable overexpression and knockdown EC cell lines, then assessed proliferation, migration, and invasion using CCK-8, wound healing, and transwell assays. Validated the cholesterol-EGFR-MEK/ERK axis through qPCR, western blotting, and non-denaturing PAGE.
  • Gained proficiency in diverse research methods, spanning bioinformatics analyses, molecular biology assays, and functional validation, while developing strong skills in experimental planning, data interpretation, and scientific reasoning.
